content_voiceover: This slide recaps the propagation phase using the classic Roman numeral notation for the coagulation factors. Notice factor seven sits off to the left, separated by a dashed line from factors eight and nine on the right. That dashed line is really separating the initiation trigger from the propagation machinery. Factor seven, paired with tissue factor, is what kicks things off and generates the first trace of factor ten a and thrombin. Once you have that initial thrombin, it feeds back and activates factors eight and nine, which then assemble together on a phospholipid surface to form the intrinsic tenase complex, and that complex is a much more efficient generator of factor ten a. Below that, you see factor ten and factor five converging on factor two, prothrombin. Factor ten a together with factor five a, calcium, and phospholipid make up the prothrombinase complex, and that's the machine that converts prothrombin into thrombin in the massive burst that defines propagation. For boards, you really want to know these two complexes cold, the intrinsic tenase built from eight and nine acting on ten, and the prothrombinase built from five and ten acting on two.
keypoints: Factor seven with tissue factor initiates the extrinsic pathway
Factors eight and nine assemble as the intrinsic tenase, activating factor ten
Factors five and ten assemble as prothrombinase, activating factor two
Dashed line separates the initiation trigger from propagation complexes
